departments.title: PLAYCRAFT — game design and gameplay quality
departments.summary: Assesses and improves how a game plays. Reads the repo (intent, engine, controls, systems with file:line evidence, genres across 15 genre profiles), plays the built game in Chromium on desktop and phone (response time of every control, dead time, idle motion, FPS, pause, touch targets, text size), scores 10 categories 0-100 with evidence levels (verified / observed / inferred / not tested) and confidence, ranks the highest-impact opportunities by impact, effort and risk, writes a staged plan, then verifies changes against the baseline (regressions + guardrails on the git diff) with a before/after report. full_pass adds GITCRAFT's engineering checks (TestCraft) under one plan.

departments.title: PIXELCRAFT — visual quality, UI/UX and interface efficiency
departments.summary: Audits the rendered application (not its source) in Chromium at iPhone 17, iPhone 13, desktop, narrow, tablet and landscape viewports: discovers its screens, captures screenshots, measures spacing, alignment, typography, touch targets, control consistency, safe areas, overflow, layout shift, hover/pressed/focus/disabled states, runs axe-core and user journeys (taps, depth, confirmations, feedback time). Scores Visual Quality, Usability and Consistency (100 each) from evidence, with coverage and confidence reported separately; every finding has screen, viewport, selector, measurements, severity, an annotated screenshot and a fix. verify replays the same routes, viewports and journeys, diffs screenshots, proves fixes and refuses score gains from lost coverage. Works on React, Vite, Next.js, static sites and browser games (HTML overlays). Never modifies the app.
departments.applies_because: PIXELCRAFT audits the rendered HTML UI of apps, sites and games

score.label: Visual quality and usability (mean of 2 UIs)

findings.title: Buttons side by side have different heights
findings.evidence: Buttons in one row are 64, 85 px tall; equivalent controls look like different components and the row looks unbalanced.
findings.recommendation: Use one button size per row (a size token: e.g. 44 px on mobile) and change emphasis with fill/outline, not padding.

findings.title: Clickable element is not a real control
findings.evidence: This element responds to clicks (pointer cursor) but is not a button or link, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot use it.
findings.recommendation: Use <button> (or <a href>) instead of a clickable <div>/<span>.

findings.title: Focusing a field zooms the page on iPhone
findings.evidence: The field's font-size is 15 px; iOS Safari zooms in on any input under 16 px and leaves the page zoomed after typing.
findings.recommendation: Use font-size: 16px (1rem) for inputs, selects and textareas on mobile.

findings.title: No pressed (active) state
findings.evidence: Pressing this control changes nothing visually until the action completes; on touch screens there is no hover, so this is the only immediate confirmation of a tap.
findings.recommendation: Add an :active style (darker tone, scale 0.97, or ripple) to every button and link variant.

findings.title: Text is too small to read comfortably
findings.evidence: 10.5-px text is below the 12-px minimum for phones; secondary information (dates, tags, captions) becomes hard to read.
findings.recommendation: Use at least 12 px (13-14 px preferred) for secondary text and keep hierarchy with weight and colour rather than very small sizes.

findings.title: Touch target is too small
findings.evidence: 228×27 px: under the 44×44 pt Apple HIG minimum (24 px is the WCAG 2.2 floor); thumbs miss and hit neighbours.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the hit area to 44×44 (padding, min-height/min-width, or an ::after hit-area) while keeping the visible glyph size.

findings.title: Touch target is too small

findings.title: Uneven spacing between related elements
findings.evidence: Items of the same kind in one list or stack are separated by different gaps, which reads as grouping that isn't there and makes the list look broken.
findings.recommendation: Give the container one gap (flex/grid `gap`, or one margin rule for all items) instead of per-item margins.

findings.title: Controls stretch across the desktop window

findings.title: Main action is at the top of the phone screen
findings.evidence: The primary action sits in the top fifth of a tall phone screen, the hardest zone to reach one-handed.
findings.recommendation: Repeat or move the main action to the lower half (a bottom action bar or floating button).

findings.title: Navigation does not show where you are
findings.evidence: On 'home' no navigation item is marked current (aria-current, selected or an active style).
findings.recommendation: Mark the current item with aria-current="page" and a visible active style.

findings.title: No hover state
findings.evidence: The pointer over this control changes nothing (colour, shadow, underline), so it does not signal that it is clickable.
findings.recommendation: Add a hover style (tone shift, underline, elevation) for every interactive component variant.

findings.title: No hover state

findings.recommendation: Add a hover style (tone shift, underline, elevation) for every interactive component variant.

findings.title: Spacing does not follow a consistent scale
findings.evidence: Paddings, gaps and margins use many unrelated values, so the rhythm between elements looks accidental rather than designed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a spacing scale (4/8-px steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) as tokens and replace one-off values with the nearest step.

findings.title: Text is cramped against the edge of its box
findings.evidence: Text inside a filled or bordered box sits within a few pixels of the edge, which looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Give boxed text at least 8 px horizontal and 4 px vertical padding (12-16 px for cards).

findings.title: Text is too small to read comfortably
findings.evidence: 11-px text is below the 12-px minimum for phones; secondary information (dates, tags, captions) becomes hard to read.
findings.recommendation: Use at least 12 px (13-14 px preferred) for secondary text and keep hierarchy with weight and colour rather than very small sizes.

findings.title: Text is truncated
findings.evidence: Content is cut off with an ellipsis or clipped; on phones important words (task names, prices) disappear.
findings.recommendation: Allow two lines (line-clamp: 2) for primary labels, or give the label the space the trailing controls take.

findings.title: The same heading level has different sizes on different screens
findings.evidence: h1 is rendered at 21, 32 px depending on the screen.
findings.recommendation: Style headings once, globally, from the type scale.

findings.title: The same heading level has different sizes on different screens
findings.evidence: h2 is rendered at 22, 26 px depending on the screen.
findings.recommendation: Style headings once, globally, from the type scale.

findings.title: Too many button variants
findings.evidence: 6 distinct button size/shape combinations (heights 32, 40, 64, 84, 248, 268 px) at iphone17: buttons were styled one by one, not from a component.
findings.recommendation: Define 2-3 button sizes and 3 emphasis levels (primary, secondary, tertiary) as one component and use it everywhere.

findings.title: Two primary actions compete
findings.evidence: 'Interact' and 'Attack' are both strongly filled, similar in size and side by side, so neither reads as the main action.
findings.recommendation: Keep one filled primary button per group; make the other secondary (outline or tonal).

departments.title: DESIGNCRAFT — game-design intelligence
departments.summary: levels, missions, story, progression and experience, from the game's own data

departments.title: TestCraft — automated QA
departments.summary: Browser QA for web games with Playwright + Chromium: smoke tests on desktop, phone and tablet emulation (errors, missing files, blank screens, overflow, canvas), scripted gameplay with assertions on game state and video capture, FPS / frame-time / heap profiling, visual regression (YIQ pixel diff, baselines), asset integrity (every file opened by format; GLBs through the Khronos validator; texture budgets), animation playback (GLB clips really move; sprite frames differ), the project's own Vitest/Jest suite, and HTML/JSON reports.
notes: 4 run(s): assets, perf, play, smoke; 26/26 output checks passed.

departments.title: AssetCraft — asset management
departments.summary: One asset catalogue for every project (SQLite in ~/.gitcraft/assetcraft): every department run registers its outputs with licence and provenance; scan existing projects; search across projects; versions on content change; exact and perceptual (dHash) duplicates; unused assets (not referenced by source); dependency tracing (glTF, Tiled, HTML/CSS); licence inventory with ATTRIBUTION.md and non-commercial flags; hash re-verification; hash-verified integration into a project (never overwriting silently); 3D-library sync; a browsable HTML catalogue.
departments.next: Catalogue the project's assets (studiocraft assetcraft_scan) for licences, duplicates and unused files.

departments.title: 3D Department — ForgeCraft + MeshCraft
notes: No 3D Department jobs reference this project.

departments.title: AnimCraft — rigging and animation
departments.summary: Automatic rigging (humanoid, quadruped, chain/tentacle/tail) from mesh landmarks with heat-map skin weights (Mixamo bone names optional); procedural clips (idle, walk, run, wave, jump; quadruped walk/run/idle; chain wave/slither/sway/curl; object bob/spin/hover/squash/shake); world-space retargeting between rigs with different names and proportions (BVH, FBX, GLB sources); rigid-body physics drops baked to keyframes; sprite sheets from 3D clips (N directions) or frame folders; playback verification in three.js.
notes: 11 run(s): animate, autorig, demo_character, physics, retarget, spritesheet; 46/46 output checks passed.

departments.title: AudioCraft — game audio
departments.summary: Sound effects, seamless ambiences, adaptive multi-stem music with MIDI source, character dialogue (Kokoro-82M neural TTS, CPU), loop-point detection, trimming, EBU R128 loudness normalisation, layering and WAV/OGG/MP3/Opus/FLAC conversion.
notes: 13 run(s): ambience, loop, music, process, sfx, voice; 23/23 output checks passed.

departments.title: CinematicCraft — cinematics and video
departments.summary: Camera choreography (orbit, dolly in/out, crane up, flyby, push-in zoom, handheld, static) over any GLB/FBX/OBJ/.blend scene with lighting presets (studio three-point, golden hour, night, overcast, dramatic, daylight) and optional HDR/equirect sky, rendered with Cycles to MP4 + editable .blend + an engine camera path (JSON) for in-game cutscenes; storyboards (PNG + PDF); animated title cards; trailer assembly with crossfades and a loudness-normalised music bed; gameplay capture from a web game.
notes: 5 run(s): assemble, capture, shot, storyboard, title_card; 13/13 output checks passed.

departments.title: FXCraft — visual effects
departments.summary: Game-ready effects: flipbook atlases from particle simulations (fire, smoke, magic, energy/portal, rain, snow loops that repeat exactly; explosion, sparks, dust, splash, lightning, debris one-shots) with Phaser/PixiJS atlas JSON, GIF and MP4 previews; portable emitter presets (.fx.json) with a dependency-free three.js runtime, played in three.js r170; three.quarks particle systems (QuarksLoader JSON); Blender Voronoi destruction with baked rigid-body physics as an animated GLB.
notes: 12 run(s): destruction, emitter, flipbook; 39/39 output checks passed.

departments.title: LevelCraft — levels and maps
departments.summary: Procedural dungeons (BSP rooms + corridors + doors), caves (cellular automata), completable platformer levels (jump-physics reachability solver), overworlds (biomes, A* roads with bridges between settlements, camps, resources) and towns (road grid, building plots with doors, plaza) — as Tiled TMJ maps and LDtk 1.5.3 projects with a generated tileset, entity/collision/navigation object layers, generic JSON, preview and a 3D blockout GLB, each solved and loaded in Phaser 3.

departments.title: MaterialCraft — PBR materials and shaders
departments.summary: Seamless procedural PBR materials (21 kinds: stone, cobblestone, brick, tiles, wood, planks, bark, metal, brushed metal, rust, fabric, leather, sand, grass, dirt, ice, lava, water, marble, concrete, snow) with dirt/moss/wear/wet weathering and a toon style; glTF metallic-roughness map sets (basecolor, normal GL/DX, roughness, metallic, AO, 16-bit height, packed ORM, emission), a sample sphere GLB, a three.js render and seam checks; seamless-izing of any image; toon gradient ramps; swatch sheets.
notes: 7 run(s): generate, library; 31/31 output checks passed.

departments.title: WorldCraft — procedural environments
departments.summary: Terrains (island, archipelago, atoll, coast, mountains, canyon, volcano, plains) with hydraulic + thermal erosion, biomes, 16-bit heightmaps, normal/splat/biome maps and masks, vegetation and rock scatter, coastlines and a vertex-coloured GLB; caves (surface-nets meshes); physical skies (Blender Nishita) as equirect + HDR + cubemap with sun lighting; seamless time-looping FFT oceans; rule-based scatter on any heightmap.
notes: 9 run(s): caves, ocean, sky, terrain; 39/39 output checks passed.
